subject: Proposal: stepwise multi-year prepay with usage-protection and SLA offset
messages:
From: Emma Frost <emma@frosthealth.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@frosthealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Multiple-year prepay idea + usage protection question

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our execs liked Redwood's latency profile and the prefix caching idea. Before we move to legal, finance asked me to explore a structure that balances our seasonal demand spikes while giving us committed savings.

High-level ask: would Redwood consider a 3-year commitment with a stepwise prepay schedule (lower prepay in year 1 to account for onboarding ramp, then larger prepay in years 2–3) plus a usage-protection clause so we don’t pay for long tails in Q1 / Q4 spikes? We also need an SLA credit if p95 latency breaches more than twice in a quarter.

I attached a quick XLS with our expected monthly profile to show seasonality. Can you run internal and let me know what flexibility you have on (a) tiered prepay amounts, (b) a modest escalator protecting Redwood economics, and (c) an SLA credit mechanism?

Cheers,
Emma
Head of Cloud Platform
Frost Health

Attachments: Frost_Proposed_Billing.xlsx (spreadsheet summary of monthly usage)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Frost <emma@frosthealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Multiple-year prepay idea + usage protection question

Emma —

Really appreciate the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Short answer: yes, we can do a 3-year stepwise prepay with protections, but there are a few knobs to align on to keep economics healthy on our side.

Proposed options to review internally:
- Option A (Conservative): Year 1 = 40% of committed ARR up-front, Year 2 = 30%, Year 3 = 30%. 10% aggregate discount vs pay-as-you-go. No escalator. Limited rollover of unused prepay (up to 10% per year).
- Option B (Balanced): Year 1 = 25% up-front, Year 2 = 35%, Year 3 = 40%. 15% aggregate discount with a 5% usage-protection reserve that covers seasonal spikes, applied as credits the following quarter.
- Option C (Accelerated): Year 1 = 15%, Year 2 = 35%, Year 3 = 50% plus a 20% aggregate discount, conditional on minimum monthly floors and a 6-month ramp protection clause.

SLA credit: we can offer a quarterly credit tied to p95 latency breaches (one free credits bucket per quarter; >2 breaches -> 5% credit against that quarter's invoice). We typically limit credits to a % of committed spend, and we need an agreed incident window and measurement metric (we report p95 per customer route in Console).

I'll need to pull in Neha on legal finance nuances and Monica for billing flow. If you’re open, I’ll outline a draft term sheet and send it back with a redline-able PDF.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Multiple-year prepay idea + usage protection question — internal pricing/approval request

Team —

Forwarding Frost Health's ask (below). Quick summary and ask: Frost wants a 3-year stepwise prepay with an explicit usage-protection mechanism and an SLA-credit. They prefer a balanced structure (Option B from my note) but are sensitive to cash timing in Y1.

Key points we should weigh:
- Year 1 lower prepay increases our capacity planning risk; suggest adding a minimum monthly floor (e.g., 60% of expected monthly consumption for first 6 months) or a smaller early prepayment but higher unit price in Y1.
- Usage-protection: we can set aside a small credits reserve (5% of committed spend) to be deployed for documented seasonal spikes; it reduces realized revenue but keeps the customer from blasting support channels.
- SLA credit caps: recommend capping credits at 10% of quarterly committed invoice; otherwise it materially erodes economics.
- Need legal input on rollover language and termination payout if they under-consume.

Can we get alignment on: (1) acceptable discount range (10–18%), (2) whether we want a 5% credits reserve for protection, and (3) SLA credit cap at 10%?

If we agree, I’ll draft a term sheet and include redlines for finance/legal.

Thanks —
Logan

Logan / Monica —

Thanks for the context. My quick take: we can approve Option B as a starting point with the following guardrails to protect our unit economics and accounting:

1) Discount band: cap at 15% aggregate for three years (we can go to 17% for enterprise credit exceptions with Finance approval).
2) Usage-protection: allow a 5% reserve that converts to credits for documented spikes; unused reserve at each anniversary rolls into a smaller rollover credit (max 5% carryover).
3) Minimum monthly floor: first 6 months have a 60% of forecast floor. If consumption is below floor, Frost pays the difference as usage true-up.
4) SLA credit: yes, tied to p95 per-route measured in Console. Cap credits at 10% of the quarterly committed invoice. Also require incident post-mortem for any credit-triggering event.

Please include these items in the draft term sheet. For billing, Monica can specify invoicing cadence (annual upfront + quarterly true-ups) and DocuSign flow.

Neha
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: stepwise multi-year prepay with usage-protection and SLA offset — term sheet and next steps

Emma —

Thanks for the patience. Per internal alignment, attached is a draft term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf) reflecting: Option B with the 15% cap, a 5% usage-protection reserve, 60% first-6-month minimum floor, and SLA credit capped at 10% of quarterly committed spend. Billing approach: annual prepay collection on Year 1 (25% of committed ARR), Year 2 prepay invoiced at start of Year 2 (35%), Year 3 prepay at start of Year 3 (40%); quarterly true-ups for consumption above committed amounts.

If that aligns, we'll push the term sheet to DocuSign and route to Legal for standard redlines. Also attaching the spreadsheet back with our annotated commentary.

Next steps:
- Emma: confirm you want Option B and we’ll prepare DocuSign (I’ll include standard ESCROW billing notes).
- Frost Contracts: please flag any mandatory legal clauses (data residency, SOC 2 evidence, indemnity limits).

Best,
Monica Patel

Redwood Inference
